Question: What is the admission process for B.Tech?
Answer: Admission to B.Tech is based on the GLAET (Entrance Test) score or CUET/JEE Main ranks, followed by counseling.

Question: How can I apply for admission?
Answer: You can apply online through the official university website by filling out the registration form and paying the application fee.

Question: What is the eligibility criteria for B.Tech?
Answer: Candidates must have passed 10+2 with Physics and Mathematics as compulsory subjects along with Chemistry/Computer Science, securing a minimum of 50% marks.

Question: Are there any scholarships available?
Answer: Yes, scholarships are provided based on 10+2 merit, entrance exam scores, and for category-specific students. Details are available on the admission portal.

Question: Can I get direct admission in the second year?
Answer: Yes, lateral entry to the second year of B.Tech is available for students holding a 3-year diploma in engineering or a B.Sc degree.

Question: What documents are required during admission?
Answer: You need your 10th and 12th mark sheets, transfer certificate, migration certificate, Aadhaar card, passport-size photos, and entrance exam scorecard.

Question: Is there a hostel facility for first-year students?
Answer: Yes, separate hostels for boys and girls are available. Rooms are allotted on a first-come, first-serve basis.

Question: What is the last date to apply for admission?
Answer: The admission deadlines vary each year. Please check the 'Important Dates' section on the university website.

Question: Can I cancel my admission and get a refund?
Answer: Yes, admission cancellation and fee refunds are processed according to the UGC refund policy. Apply through the admissions office.

Question: Where is the admission cell located?
Answer: The admission cell is located in the main administrative block on the ground floor.

Question: How do I pay my semester fees?
Answer: Semester fees can be paid online through the student ERP portal using UPI, Net Banking, or Debit/Credit Cards.

Question: What is the deadline for fee payment?
Answer: The fee payment deadline is usually two weeks before the start of the new semester. Exact dates are mailed to your student ID.

Question: Is there a fine for late fee payment?
Answer: Yes, a late fine of Rs. 100 per day is charged if the fee is not paid by the specified deadline.

Question: Can I pay my tuition fees in installments?
Answer: Generally, fees must be paid semester-wise. Installment requests are only approved under special financial circumstances by the Finance Officer.

Question: How can I download my fee receipt?
Answer: You can download your official fee receipt directly from the 'Fee Details' section in your student ERP dashboard.

Question: What is the hostel and mess fee structure?
Answer: Hostel and mess fees vary based on the room type (AC/Non-AC, Single/Double occupancy). Please check the hostel brochure for exact amounts.

Question: Does the college provide documents for an education loan?
Answer: Yes, the accounts department provides a fee structure letter and a bonafide certificate for students applying for education loans.

Question: Are there any extra charges for bus facilities?
Answer: Yes, transport fees are separate from academic fees and depend on your boarding location.

Question: What should I do if my fee payment fails but money is deducted?
Answer: Wait for 24 hours. If it is not updated on the ERP, email the transaction ID and screenshot to the finance department.

Question: Is the caution money refundable?
Answer: Yes, the caution deposit is fully refundable at the end of your degree after obtaining a no-dues certificate.

Question: When will the mid-semester exams begin?
Answer: Mid-semester exams are typically scheduled in the 8th week of the semester. Check the academic calendar for exact dates.

Question: Where can I download my exam admit card?
Answer: Admit cards can be downloaded from the student ERP portal three days before the commencement of exams.

Question: What is the minimum passing marks criteria?
Answer: A student must secure at least 30% in the end-semester exam and an overall 40% (internal + external) to pass a subject.

Question: What happens if I fail an exam?
Answer: If you fail an exam, you will get a 'Back Paper' (carry-over). You must fill out the carry-over form and reappear for the exam next year.

Question: How do I apply for re-evaluation of my answer sheet?
Answer: Re-evaluation forms are available on the ERP portal for a limited time after results are declared. A nominal fee is charged per subject.

Question: Can I miss my internal exams due to medical reasons?
Answer: If you miss an internal exam due to a severe medical emergency, submit a medical certificate to your HOD immediately for consideration.

Question: Where can I find the syllabus for my branch?
Answer: The complete syllabus and course structure are available in the department section of the university website and on the LMS.

Question: When will the final semester results be declared?
Answer: Results are usually declared within 30 to 45 days after the last date of the end-semester examinations.

Question: How is my CGPA calculated?
Answer: CGPA is the credit-weighted average of the grade points you earn across all semesters. The formula is available in the student rulebook.

Question: Are calculators allowed in the examination hall?
Answer: Non-programmable scientific calculators are allowed only for specific numerical-heavy subjects, as instructed by the invigilator.

Question: Where can I check my class timetable?
Answer: The class timetable is uploaded to your student ERP account and is also pinned on the department notice board.

Question: What are the regular college timings?
Answer: Regular college hours are from 9:00 AM to 4:30 PM, Monday through Friday. Saturdays may have special labs or clubs.

Question: What is the minimum attendance requirement?
Answer: Students must maintain a minimum of 75% attendance in each subject to be eligible to sit for the end-semester exams.

Question: Where can I get the list of college holidays?
Answer: The official academic calendar, which includes the list of all holidays, is available on the university website and ERP.

Question: What are the library timings?
Answer: The central library is open from 8:00 AM to 8:00 PM on working days, and up to 10:00 PM during examination weeks.

Question: Can I change my branch after the first year?
Answer: Branch sliding is possible after the first year based on seat availability and your first-year CGPA (usually requiring 8.0+).

Question: How do I contact my Head of Department (HOD)?
Answer: You can meet your HOD during their designated meeting hours or email them at their official university email address.

Question: I forgot my ERP password, how do I reset it?
Answer: Click on 'Forgot Password' on the ERP login page. An OTP will be sent to your registered mobile number and email.

Question: How do I access the college Wi-Fi?
Answer: Connect to the campus network and log in using your student ID and the Wi-Fi password provided by the IT department.

Question: Are there any extra classes for weak students?
Answer: Yes, remedial classes are scheduled by respective faculty members for students who need extra academic support.

Question: Where is the college located?
Answer: GLA University is located on the Delhi-Mathura Highway (NH-2), Chaumuhan, Mathura, Uttar Pradesh.

Question: What is the dress code or uniform policy?
Answer: Students must wear the prescribed university uniform on specified days and formal/smart casuals on other days. ID cards are mandatory.

Question: Does the college have a medical dispensary?
Answer: Yes, there is a 24/7 campus dispensary with a resident doctor and an ambulance available for medical emergencies.

Question: How are the placement records of the college?
Answer: The university has a strong placement record with a dedicated Training & Placement cell. Top MNCs visit annually. Check the placement portal for stats.

Question: How can I join student clubs and societies?
Answer: You can join technical and cultural clubs during the annual club recruitment drive held at the beginning of the odd semester.

Question: What are the sports facilities available?
Answer: The campus features grounds for cricket, football, basketball, badminton, and a fully equipped indoor sports complex and gym.

Question: How do I report an incident of ragging?
Answer: Ragging is strictly prohibited. You can contact the Anti-Ragging toll-free helpline or immediately report it to your mentor or the Chief Warden.

Question: I lost my ID card, how do I get a new one?
Answer: File an application with the admin office, attach a copy of an FIR/police complaint, and pay the duplicate ID card fee to get a replacement.

Question: Where is the student grievance cell?
Answer: The student grievance redressal cell operates from the Dean of Student Welfare (DSW) office. You can also file grievances online via the ERP.

Question: Can I bring my personal vehicle to campus?
Answer: Day scholars can bring two-wheelers and park them in the designated student parking area by showing their college ID.
